note: Mission Composer layer 4 (vision plan 4.2): turns. A twist lands mid-mission and always offers a choice whose answer becomes story (arc outcome and a deed). Hail lines are hand-written; {requester} and {target} are filled in code. wrong_cargo reveals a courier's sealed container mid-flight (N.O.V.A. scans it) and asks: deliver anyway, or dump it. client_lie reveals the requester's private fact mid-job (finish anyway, or expose them). rival_on_the_job: a rival pilot on the same contract (split the fee, or race against a clock; lose the race and the rival takes the credit). stowaway: someone hid in the hold (shelter them, or turn them in for a bounty). double_booking: another party paid for the same cargo (keep the job, or switch and get paid now; the job is dropped). law_change: a new local law makes the run illegal (pay the duty, or run it and risk a fine from a patrol scan).

hails: Hold fire. Whatever {requester} is paying you, I can beat it. Take my money and let me go, and nobody has to know.
Wait. Before you finish this, ask yourself why {requester} wants me dead and not in a cell. I'll pay more than they will.
Cease fire. I'm not the story you were sold. Walk away from {requester}'s job and I'll make it worth your while.
Listen. {requester} is using you to clean up their mess. I can pay you better than they can, right now, clean.
I'm powering down. Weapons cold. You've won. Please, just let me go home.
Stop, please. I surrender. My drives are dead and I've got people waiting for me. You don't have to do this.
All right, it's over, I yield. Shields down, guns off. I'll leave this system and never come back. Just let me live.
Don't. I'm done, I'm out. Whatever {requester} told you about me, I'm not worth the shot.

true_cargo: weapon parts with the serials burned off
hails: Captain, the mass on that container is wrong for {item}. I scanned it. It's {true_cargo}. {requester} didn't mention that.
I don't like surprises, so here's one I found: that sealed crate isn't {item}. It's {true_cargo}.
Before we get there: the manifest says {item}. The scan says {true_cargo}. One of those is lying, and it isn't the scanner.
Captain, I went through {requester}'s traffic while we flew. Here's what they left out: {fact}
You should hear this before we finish. {fact} That's who we're working for.
I don't think {requester} told us the whole story. {fact}
{rival} here. Same contract as you, pilot. {requester} hired us both and pays whoever finishes first. Split it with me, or race me for it.
Well, well. {rival}, working the same job for {requester}. We can share the fee and both go home, or you can try to beat me there.
You're on {requester}'s job too? Of course you are. This is {rival}. Half each, or the fast one takes it all. Your call.
Captain, there's a heartbeat in the hold that isn't yours. Someone called {stranger} stowed away before we launched. They're asking us not to hand them over.
We have a passenger. {stranger}, hiding behind the cargo since the dock. They say they had to get out, and they're begging for a quiet drop-off.
Life support's working for two. There's a stowaway aboard, {stranger}. There's a standing bounty on runaways, or we could let them off quietly at the drop.
This is {stranger}. We paid for this cargo too, pilot, and it's not going to {requester}. Bring it to us instead and the fee's yours now, in full.
{stranger} here. Someone sold this job twice, and we were first. Turn around, hand it to us, and we'll pay what {requester} promised, today.
Pilot, {stranger}. {requester} doesn't own that cargo, we do, and we already paid for its delivery. Switch to us and get paid now. Or don't, and remember who you crossed.

laws: an emergency ban on unlicensed freight
a new duty on anything moving through the lanes
a lockdown on shipments from outside the system
hails: Captain, the local authority just declared {law}. As of now our run is illegal unless we pay the duty.
News on the local band: {law}, effective now. We can pay the duty and stay clean, or keep flying and hope nobody scans us.
Timing. They just announced {law}. Pay up and it's legal. Don't, and every patrol in the system has a reason to stop us.
